sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 29–35)
points: Lesson 29: "Tafura iyi inoda kupukutwa nokuti vana varasira mukaka pairi." — This table needs to be wiped because the children spilled milk on it.
Lesson 30: "Ndachengeta mari shoma; kuti ndigozotenge zvimwe zvinhu mangwana." — I have saved a little money so that I can buy some other things tomorrow.
Lesson 31: "Ndakanganwa penzura yangu kumba asi shamwari yangu yandibatsira." — I forgot my pencil at home, but my friend helped me.
Lesson 32: "Chingwa chapera saka ndichapfuura nekuchitoro pandinobva kubasa." — The bread has run out, so I will pass by the store when I leave work.
Lesson 33: "Tine maminitsi mashanu chete saka ngatikurumidze kupedza zvatirikuita." — We only have five minutes, so let us hurry and finish what we are doing.
Lesson 34: "Vakuru vanoti, "Chara chimwe hachitswanyi inda."" — The elders say, "One finger cannot crush a louse."
Lesson 35: "Mwana ari kuchema mumba nokuti arumwa nenyuchi." — The child is crying in the house because he was stung by a bee.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('inoda'): [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)
Connecting Clauses & Expressing Purpose with 'kuti': kuti + [Subject Prefix + Verb ending in -e] = 'so that [someone] may...' (e.g., kuti tidye = so that we eat)
Talking About the Past ('Ndakanganwa'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('chapera'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Counting & Numbers in Shona ('mashanu'): Noun + Number Stem (-mwe = 1, -viri = 2, -tatu = 3, -na = 4, -shanu = 5) -> vanhu vaviri (2 people), maminitsi mashanu (5 minutes)
Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('vanoti'): [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Keeping the Family Dining Table ('Tafura') Spotless: Cleanliness ('utsanana') in the kitchen and dining room is a point of pride in Shona homes: tables are wiped down ('kupukutwa') immediately before and after children have their morning milk ('mukaka') and porridge..

Household Budgeting & Saving ('Kuchengeta Mari') for Market Days: Careful household budgeting—setting aside small savings ('kuchengeta mari shoma') or participating in community savings clubs ('mukando' / 'marounds')—helps families purchase groceries and school supplies without strain..

Classroom Camaraderie & Sharing Stationery ('Penzura') at School: In Zimbabwean primary and secondary schools, classmates readily share pencils ('penzura'), pens ('zvinyoreso'), and rulers when a friend forgets theirs at home, fostering lifelong school friendships ('ushamwari hwepachikoro')..
Neighbourhood Grocery Stores ('Zvitoro') & Fresh Daily Bread: Freshly baked loaves of bread ('chingwa') from local bakeries like Lobels or Proton are a daily staple in Zimbabwean homes.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 5 — Concessive Clauses ('Kunyangwe'): Which sentence means 'Even though the river is wide, they crossed safely'?
options: Kana rwizi rwuzere, hatigoni kuyambuka nhasi.
Rwizi urwu runoyerera ruchienda kumabvazuva.
Vana vari kutamba pedyo nerwizi.
Kunyangwe rwizi rwakafara, vakayambuka zvakanaka.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Kunyangwe' introduces an 'although / even though' clause, followed by 'vakayambuka zvakanaka' ('they crossed safely').

review_exercises.prompt: Review 5 — Relative Clauses: What does ' nzira inoenda kumunda' mean?
options: the path that goes to the field
we are walking along the path
the field is far from the road
go to the field tomorrow morning
review_exercises.correct_answer: the path that goes to the field
review_exercises.explanation: 'Inoenda' acts as a relative verb modifying 'nzira' ('path') -> 'the path which goes'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 5 — Passive Voice ('-wa'): How do you say 'The maize was planted in November'?
options: Varimi vanodyara chibage muna Mbudzi.
Chibage chakadyarwa muna Mbudzi.
Tichadyara chibage kana mvura yanaya.
Chibage chiri kukura zvakanaka mumunda.
review_exercises.explanation: Adding '-wa' to '-dyara' (plant) forms the passive '-dyarwa' ('was planted').

review_exercises.prompt: Review 5 — Reflexive Prefix ('-zvi-'): In 'Anofanira kuzvibata zvakanaka', what does '-zvi-' do?
options: It makes the verb negative
It refers to plural objects on the table
It means 'himself / herself / oneself' (to conduct oneself well)
It indicates the distant past tense
review_exercises.correct_answer: It means 'himself / herself / oneself' (to conduct oneself well)
review_exercises.explanation: The reflexive prefix '-zvi-' placed right before the verb stem means 'oneself' ('kuzvibata' = to behave/control oneself).

review_exercises.prompt: Review 5 — Farming & Harvest: What is the meaning of 'Tarisiro yedu ndeyekuwana goho guru gore rino'?
options: We already sold all our harvest at the market
Last year the rain was very scarce in our village
The farmers are repairing their tools in the yard
Our hope is to obtain a bountiful harvest this year
review_exercises.correct_answer: Our hope is to obtain a bountiful harvest this year
review_exercises.explanation: 'Tarisiro yedu' = 'Our hope/expectation', 'ndeyekuwana goho guru' = 'is to obtain a big harvest', 'gore rino' = 'this year'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 5 — Translate this new review sentence: 'Mvura yakanaya usiku hwese saka ivhu rakanyorova.'
options: It rained all night long, so the soil is moist.
The sun shone brightly all day and dried the grass.
We will plant groundnuts and maize next week.
The river water is clean and cool in the morning.
review_exercises.correct_answer: It rained all night long, so the soil is moist.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Mvura yakanaya usiku hwese' = 'It rained the whole night', 'saka' = 'so', 'ivhu rakanyorova' = 'the soil is wet/moist'.
